description: We are a multidisciplinary team of 6 students from CUGDL (University of Guadalajara) in Mexico, combining 5 Biomedical Technologies majors and 1 Financial Technologies major. We are participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 to gain hands-on experience, learn from real-world space challenges, and collaborate on innovative solutions. Our team is currently complete, and we are excited to bring our passion, curiosity, and fresh perspectives!
summary:
We developed 'Operation: Echoes of Lunar Dust,' an interactive 3D web experience that works like a digital rescue museum. To tackle the challenge, we transformed the common perception of past mission hardware as simple 'space junk' into a living archive. Through an immersive interface with a space terminal aesthetic, users can inspect official NASA 3D models (like the Apollo Lunar Module and the Rovers) and unlock their historical logs along with real telemetry data.

This project is important because it humanizes space exploration. By combining scientific rigor with an emotional narrative, we manage to generate empathy in new generations towards engineering, ensuring that the legacy of these silent guardians continues to inspire the future.
details:
Cómo funciona: Es un museo web 3D con una interfaz de terminal espacial donde los usuarios exploran artefactos lunares y desbloquean su historia real y telemetría.

Impacto y beneficios: Cambia la percepción pública de la 'basura espacial', presentándola como 'guardianes silenciosos'. Esto democratiza el acceso al patrimonio lunar, educando y creando empatía por la ciencia desde cualquier usuario.

Tecnología utilizada: HTML, CSS y JavaScript (en VS Code), modelos oficiales 3D de la NASA (. GLB), Netlify para alojamiento web y Gemini como asistente de desarrollo.

Creatividad: Sustituye el aburrido estilo enciclopédico por una experiencia inmersiva y emocional (estética oscura, narrativa humanizada, audio ambiental), manteniendo siempre la precisión histórica y la accesibilidad técnica.
